title: Built-in MCP OAuth server when Clerk is off (connectors need OAuth once keys leave URLs)
acceptance: the gateway answers 401 with a WWW-Authenticate header naming its protected resource metadata (RFC 9728, at both the path-inserted and the root well-known URI). Authorization server metadata is served by RFC 8414 and by OIDC discovery with an exact issuer, and the authorization response returns iss

clients register by Client ID Metadata Document (advertised with client_id_metadata_document_supported, fetched with SSRF guards), with dynamic client registration only as a deprecated fallback. PKCE S256 is required and advertised. The resource parameter is required, and the token's audience is the gateway's own MCP address. A call with insufficient scope gets 403 so the client can step up
access tokens are short-lived and workspace-scoped, refresh tokens rotate, and the consent screen names the client and the workspace
